claims.statement: Kensington and Chelsea Council faces a projected £127 million funding gap over the next four years.
claims.sourceQuote: Kensington and Chelsea Council is facing a projected £127 million funding gap over the next four years, prompting warnings of potential council tax hikes.
claims.sourceDocument: Full Council Kensington and Chelsea, 21 October 2026

claims.statement: The council is submitting a cross-party proposal to the Treasury backed by 1,500 residents.
claims.sourceQuote: Tomorrow morning, together with other leaders from across London, we're taking that submission to the Treasury. She emphasised that this is not a party political fight, with the council's case supported by Liberal Democrats, Conservatives, and Greens, as well as 1,500 residents and thousands of businesses.
claims.sourceDocument: Full Council Kensington and Chelsea, 21 October 2026

claims.statement: Labour councillors advocate retaining up to 50% of the new high-value council tax surcharge.
claims.sourceQuote: Instead, their approach is to advocating, along with London councils and our local MPs, that the transition be softened and lengthened by allowing inner London boroughs to retain up to 50% of the new high-value council tax surcharge and a larger percentage of our business rates during this transition period.
claims.sourceDocument: Full Council Kensington and Chelsea, 21 October 2026

takeawayCard.title: Council fights government cuts
takeawayCard.subtitle: Cross-party coalition petitions Treasury for relief.

keyPoints: Kensington faces a projected £127 million budget gap over four years.
Leaders take a joint submission directly to the Treasury.
Labour councillors suggest retaining half of high-value council tax surcharges.
